solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Chief catches barman perhaps nicking last drink (10)

indicatorNotes.catches: the chief holds the composer inside himself
indicatorNotes.nicking last: to nick is to steal, so the name's final letter is taken

blocks.note: a capo is a Mafia chief; it opens around the next piece
PUCCINI, a composer who writes in bars, without his last letter

annotation.surface: A crime boss catches the barman pilfering the last drink from the bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Barman' is not a bartender but a composer, whose music is written in bars; Puccini is the example here.
annotation.definitionFit: An Italian espresso topped with frothed milk, ordered as a drink in any café.

entries.clue: Batman outfit‘s carbon copy (4)

annotation.surface: Someone owns a knock-off of the Batman costume.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carbon copy' looks like one phrase but splits into two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: The sleeveless cloak is the signature piece of the caped crusader's costume, a definition by part.

entries.clue: Nutty thing keeping left on one particular crossing (7)

indicatorNotes.keeping: the nut holds the letters inside it
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, L sits on top of I

blocks.note: a pecan is a nut; it opens around the next pieces

annotation.surface: A nutty person keeps left at a particular crossing.
annotation.walkthrough: A pelican crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with lights the walker controls by button.
annotation.definitionFit: British road crossings are named by type, zebra, puffin and this one, so the bird names a particular crossing.

entries.clue: Drama below par that’s possibly skimmed on plane? (5,4,4)

blocks.note: a drink that may be skimmed of its cream
the plane is a tree, so its timber

annotation.surface: A play feels below par, like something only skimmed on a flight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aeroplane but is the tree; Under Milk Wood is Dylan Thomas's radio play.
annotation.definitionFit: Dylan Thomas's 'play for voices' is a drama by example.

entries.clue: Crew tracking blue sharks (6)

indicatorNotes.tracking: to track is to follow, so the crew comes after

blocks.note: blue is the Conservative colour, so CON

annotation.surface: A boat crew follows a school of blue sharks.
annotation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative party, abbreviated CON. 'Sharks' reads as fish but means swindlers.
annotation.definitionFit: A shark in the human sense is a swindler who preys on the gullible.

entries.clue: Harry outside curses, scrubbing innermost boat (5,3)

indicatorNotes.outside: the first word goes around the second
indicatorNotes.scrubbing innermost: scrubbing removes; the innermost letter is the middle one

blocks.note: to harry or annoy is to nark; it goes around the next piece

annotation.surface: Harry, out on deck, swears while scrubbing the inside of a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a man's name but is a verb, to nag.
annotation.definitionFit: The vessel of the Flood story in Genesis is a boat by example.

entries.clue: Image of faceless suit (1-3)

indicatorNotes.faceless: without its face, the front letter is lost

annotation.surface: A picture of a suit with no face, like a mannequin.
annotation.walkthrough: An e-fit is a computer-built picture of a suspect's face, which makes 'faceless' neatly ironic.
annotation.definitionFit: Police build a suspect's likeness on computer from witness descriptions, an image.

entries.clue: Cinema bound to invest in sound (7)

indicatorNotes.to invest in: to invest is to put inside, so LEAP goes into FIT

blocks.note: sound in body is fit; it holds the next piece

annotation.surface: A cinema is obliged to spend money on its sound system.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as obliged and 'sound' as audio; both are something else. A fleapit is a shabby old cinema.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang for a shabby, run-down picture house, supposedly infested with insects.

entries.clue: Paparazzo ultimately underlining The Sun’s daily activity: guesswork (10)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: at the end, so the last letter
indicatorNotes.underlining: in a down clue, the O sits underneath THE

blocks.note: the sun comes up each morning

annotation.surface: A photographer's work supports a tabloid's daily gossip, all guesswork.
annotation.walkthrough: The Sun looks like the British tabloid newspaper, which suits the paparazzo, but it is the star that comes up daily.
annotation.definitionFit: Speculating without firm proof is guesswork, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Knight advanced row, pursuing mate (7)

indicatorNotes.pursuing: coming after, so A and DIN follow PAL

blocks.note: a row, rhyming with cow, is a noisy din

annotation.surface: A knight moved forward in a chess row, chasing checkmate.
annotation.walkthrough: The chess picture (knight, advanced, mate) is a decoy: 'row' is a noise, not a rank of squares.
annotation.definitionFit: Charlemagne's twelve peers were knightly champions, and the word spread to any chivalrous knight.

entries.clue: Plain overcoat left out in case of amble (7)

indicatorNotes.left out: 'left' is L, and 'out' means it is dropped from the word
indicatorNotes.in: the coat goes inside the case
indicatorNotes.case of: the outside letters of a word are its case

blocks.note: first and last letters of amble; they go around the next piece
ULSTER, a long overcoat, without L

annotation.surface: Someone takes a plain overcoat off for a stroll.
annotation.walkthrough: An ulster is a long, heavy overcoat named after the Irish province.
annotation.definitionFit: Severe and unadorned in style, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: With Zoom, face Heather, making quick contact (5,8)

blocks.note: a clock's face is its dial

annotation.surface: Someone faces a colleague called Heather on a Zoom video call.
annotation.walkthrough: Zoom looks like the video-call app and Heather like a woman; they are a verb and a plant.
annotation.definitionFit: Calling a stored number with one button is a quick way of getting in touch.

entries.clue: What manager may do if defender errs in domestic fixture? (6-7)

annotation.definition2: What manager may do if defender errs

blocks.clueFragment: What manager may do if defender errs
blocks.note: to carpet is to reprimand; a sweeper is a defender in football

annotation.surface: A football manager reacts when a defender blunders in a home match.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'domestic fixture' sounds like a league match; it is a household gadget. To carpet someone is to haul them in for a telling-off.
annotation.definitionFit: A manager reprimands (carpets) an erring last defender; separately, the rug-cleaning gadget is a household fixture.

entries.clue: In time, is Asda maybe making a series of bloomers (5,5)

indicatorNotes.In: IS goes inside the word for time

blocks.note: a day is a time; it holds the next piece
Asda is a British supermarket chain

annotation.surface: A supermarket keeps making blunders, one after another.
annotation.walkthrough: Asda is a British supermarket chain. 'Bloomers' suggests blunders or underwear, but here they are flowers.
annotation.definitionFit: Children thread flowers stalk to stalk into a garland: a string of things that bloom.

entries.clue: Top-class free broadcaster (6)

annotation.surface: A superb broadcaster that costs nothing to watch.
annotation.walkthrough: Auntie is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC.
annotation.definitionFit: The BBC's affectionate nickname stands for Britain's public broadcaster.

entries.clue: Mentions entertaining round, consistently missing greens? (8)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: to entertain is to hold, so CITES goes around
indicatorNotes.consistently missing: missing at a steady interval, so every other letter goes

blocks.note: to mention is to cite; it holds the next piece
R_U_D, every other letter of round

annotation.surface: Someone mentions buying a round while always skipping the vegetables.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a round of drinks; only its alternate letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: Raw vegetable sticks served with dips are loosely greens, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Botanist initially raising passion fruit reported condition (8)

indicatorNotes.initially: at the start, so the first letter
indicatorNotes.raising: in a down clue, lifting a word reverses it
indicatorNotes.reported: heard rather than read, so the fruit is sounded

annotation.surface: A botanist who grows passion fruit describes the plant's state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passion fruit' reads as one thing but splits: passion is anger, fruit is a berry.
annotation.definitionFit: A disease caused by lack of vitamin B1, a medical condition.

entries.clue: Trainer embracing international archer? (8)

indicatorNotes.embracing: wrapping arms around, so I goes inside

blocks.note: a trainer is a sneaker; it holds the next piece

annotation.surface: A coach hugs an archer who competes internationally.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Archer' is not a bowman but the comparative of arch (sly), which the question mark flags.
annotation.definitionFit: Arch means sly, so its comparative means slyer, more underhand.

entries.clue: European found divorce a morale-booster (3-4)

blocks.note: found, as in obtained, is got
to divorce is to tear apart, rip

annotation.surface: A European finds that getting divorced lifts the spirits.
annotation.walkthrough: An ego trip is self-indulgent activity that flatters one's self-image.
annotation.definitionFit: Self-flattering activity lifts one's self-esteem, so it boosts morale.

entries.clue: Favourite skirt and jacket of oarswoman (6)

indicatorNotes.jacket of: a jacket covers the outside, so the first and last letters

annotation.surface: A rower's favourite outfit is a skirt and jacket.
annotation.walkthrough: A minion is originally a favourite, a court darling, before it meant an underling.
annotation.definitionFit: The older sense, from French mignon (darling), is a patron's pet or favourite.

entries.clue: Painting for me to frame after (7)

indicatorNotes.to frame: a frame goes around, so IMO surrounds PAST

blocks.note: 'in my opinion', texting shorthand; it holds the next piece
after, as in half past, is past

annotation.surface: Someone wants a painting framed later on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Frame' belongs in a gallery here, but it is only the container signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Laying paint on thickly so brushstrokes stand out is a painting technique.

entries.clue: Endless relay in sports car over one frozen course (6)

indicatorNotes.Endless: a word with no ends has lost its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.in: the trimmed word goes inside the car
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, the car sits above I

blocks.note: a GT is a sports car; it holds the next piece
RELAY without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A relay race run in sports cars over an icy track.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Frozen course' suggests an icy racetrack; it is a dessert course.
annotation.definitionFit: Italian ice creams served as dessert make a frozen course of a meal.

entries.clue: One grasps snappy creature with lead on cliff edge (9,4)

indicatorNotes.lead on: the leading letter of the next word

blocks.note: a reptile that snaps its jaws

annotation.surface: A snapping crocodile, on a leash, clings to the cliff edge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a leash, which suits the crocodile, but it points to a first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: The toothed spring clip used in electrics grasps a wire, so 'one grasps' describes it.

entries.clue: Skinny latte’s essential ingredient for chap (4)

indicatorNotes.essential ingredient: the essence of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: the skinny is inside information, gen

annotation.surface: Espresso is the key part of a skinny latte ordered for a man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Skinny' looks like low-fat milk but is a noun, informal for the facts, like gen.
annotation.definitionFit: Short for gentleman, it is an informal word for a man, just as chap is.

entries.clue: Contract period to receive book delivered (7)

indicatorNotes.to receive: the period takes the other letters inside

blocks.note: an age is a period; it holds the next pieces

annotation.surface: An employment contract runs a period before a book is handed over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contract' is a verb, to shorten, not a legal document.
annotation.definitionFit: Shortening a text is making it contract, a plain synonym for the verb.

entries.clue: Audi’s original wiper in question (2,5)

indicatorNotes.original: the origin of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a paper handkerchief used for wiping a nose

annotation.surface: The original windscreen wiper on an Audi car is being queried.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wiper' suggests a car windscreen part because of Audi, but it is a paper hanky.
annotation.definitionFit: A matter under debate is the one being questioned, an idiom.

entries.clue: Scruff in a peasant’s clothing (4)

indicatorNotes.clothing: the words clothe, or wrap, the answer

blocks.note: runs from the end of 'in' into the start of 'peasant'

annotation.surface: A scruffy person dressed in a peasant's clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scruff' reads as a scruffy person, but it is the back of the neck, as in scruff of the neck.
annotation.definitionFit: The scruff, as in 'by the scruff of the neck', is the back of the neck.

entries.clue: Yorkshire Division B excessively retracted footwear (6,4)

indicatorNotes.retracted: drawn back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: Yorkshire was divided into three Ridings

annotation.surface: A Yorkshire football team in Division B pulled back too far.
annotation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, an English county, was historically split into North, East and West Ridings.
annotation.definitionFit: A tall leather boot worn on horseback is footwear by example.
